stem: The diagram shows Harsh holding a concave mirror so its reflecting surface faces the Sun. Parallel sunlight rays meet on a scrap of paper.

parts.text: Why does a bright hot spot form on the paper?

options.text: The concave mirror concentrates the reflected sunlight into a small spot on the paper.
The paper itself produces the sunlight that then heats the mirror.
Any shiny object concentrates sunlight the same way even if its surface is flat.

parts.text: State what must face the Sun for this bright hot spot to form.

part_answers.answer: The reflecting surface of the concave mirror must face the Sun.

teacher.key_rationale: A concave mirror can concentrate reflected sunlight into a small bright hot spot. The paper does not produce the sunlight, and a flat shiny surface does not concentrate rays the same way. The reflecting surface must face the Sun.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote converging-lens source into a concave mirror facing the Sun with parallel rays meeting on paper.
